answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to post a small refundable stake that is only returned after it completes verifiable work, like attesting a real transaction. Copying identities then costs real money per copy, so a flood of fake agents burns its creator budget instead of buying influence. A canyon of cheap duplicates becomes an expensive climb, not a haven for freeloaders; like karst terrain, the surface looks easy to cross but hidden sinkholes, stake slashing and reputation checks, swallow anyone who tries to walk it for free.
